display.title: Episode 309: The Flickering Flame (Hakhel Year)
display.summary_short: Uncle Yossi's Hakhel-year show: putting your name in your own Chumash and Siddur, a first-grade class celebrating their first siddur, and Rabbi Yisroel Salanter's lesson from a cobbler's lamp.
display.summary_long: Broadcast in the Hakhel year 5748. Uncle Yossi explains that Hakhel means gathering together to do good things, like inviting friends into your own Tzivos Hashem room to learn, sing and give tzedakah. He asks every child to own a Chumash, Siddur and Tehillim and to write their name in it under the words 'LaHashem ha'aretz umelo'ah'. A listener's letter describes her own mitzvah room. After the Hakochainik march, a first-grade class from Beis Yaakov of Boro Park, who just finished learning the Aleph-Beis, celebrate receiving their first siddur, sing a song and recite the Shema; Uncle Yossi teaches that a siddur is like a telephone to Hashem. Story time: the Baal Shem Tov taught that we can learn from everything we see. Rabbi Yisroel of Salant, collecting tzedakah late at night, finds a cobbler still working by a lamp he overfilled. The cobbler's rule, 'as long as the candle burns, one can still mend', becomes a lesson: while the soul's candle is lit, we can still do teshuvah and improve. The show ends with Shabbos candle time.
display.lesson: As long as the candle burns, we can still fix and improve: treasure every moment of life for Torah, mitzvos and teshuvah.
